Appearance:

sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1. Rule.
Learned APP waives service of notice of Rule for and on behalf of respondent - State.

2. The present application is filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for regular bail in connection with C.R.No.11210022232079 of 2023 registered with Kapodra Police Station, District Surat for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 143, 376, 376(2)(j)(n) and 376(3) of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3(A), 4, 5(L), 6, 7, 8, 16 and 17 of the POCSO Act.

3. Heard learned advocate Ms. Sarika Salve for the applicant and learned APP Ms. Divyangna Jhala for the respondent - State.

sentences.text: 4. Learned advocate Ms. Salve for the applicant NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/3022/2024 ORDER DATED: 15/02/2024 undefined submits that considering the nature of the offence, the applicant may be enlarged on regular bail by imposing suitable conditions.
It is submitted that applicant has been arrested on 16.11.2023 and since then he is in judicial custody.
It is further submitted that investigation is already concluded and present application is filed after submission of charge- sheet.
Learned advocate Ms. Salve further submits that FIR is filed by the mother of the victim and at the time of incident, the age of the victim was 15 years and 9 months.

It is further submitted that during the course of investigation, investigating officer has recorded the statement of the victim, wherein, she has stated in very categoric terms that they were in relationship since last more than 2 years and they eloped together at Madhya Pradesh and stayed there for three days and it is further stated that during their stay at Madhya Pradesh, applicant has not done anything wrong with her.

It is further submitted that during the course of investigation, the investigating officer has also sent certain articles to the FSL and if this Court would go through the report of the FSL, in that event, it would be found out that involvement of the present applicant accused in commission of crime is not found out.
Learned advocate Ms. Salve further submits that the applicant and victim both had NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/3022/2024 ORDER DATED: 15/02/2024 undefined gone together with a sole intent to get married.
The applicant accused has no past antecedent and age of the applicant is 18 years.
Learned advocate Ms. Salve further submits that charge- sheet is already filed before the competent Court and therefore there is no chance of tampering with the evidence.
Moreover, number of cases are pending before the concerned Trial Court and therefore it would take considerably long time to conclude the trial.
Thus, considering the above stated factual aspects, applicant may be enlarged on bail by imposing stringent conditions.
5. On the other hand, learned APP Ms. Jhala appearing on behalf of the respondent-State has opposed grant of regular bail looking to the nature and gravity of the offence.
It is further submitted that involvement of the present applicant is found out from day one of the incident.
The FIR has been filed by the mother of the victim wherein name of the present applicant accused is mentioned.

Learned APP Ms. Jhala further submits that it is well within the knowledge of the applicant accused that age of the victim is 15 years and 9 months and she was minor even though he has abducted her from the custody of her parents.

Not only that thereafter he has developed physical relationship with her against her wish and volition and said fact is clearly found out from the statement of the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/3022/2024 ORDER DATED: 15/02/2024 undefined victim which was recorded by the IO wherein she has very categorically stated that against her wish and will, two to three occasions, applicant accused has used force and developed physical relationship.

Thus,
considering the aforesaid factual aspects, applicant may not be enlarged on bail.

6. Having heard the learned advocates appearing for both the parties and having gone through the material produced on record, it is found out that FIR being C.R.No.11210022232079 of 2023 came to be registered against the applicant accused with Kapodra Police Station, District Surat for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 143, 376, 376(2)(j)(n) and 376(3) of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3(A), 4, 5(L), 6, 7, 8, 16 and 17 of the POCSO Act.
In connection with the said offence, applicant came to be arrested on 16.11.2023 and since then he is in judicial custody.
It is also found out from the record that investigation is already concluded and charge-sheet is also filed.
It is not in dispute that the age of the victim girl at the time of incident was 15 years and 9 months.

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Apex Court has further observed in Paragraphs 10 and 16 as under;
"10.
In our opinion none of the aforesaid decisions can be said to have laid down any absolute and unconditional rule about when bail should be granted by the Court and when it should not.
It all depends on the facts and circumstances of each case and it cannot be said there is any absolute rule that because a long period of imprisonment has expired bail must necessarily be granted.

16. We are of the opinion that while it is true that Article 21 is of great importance because it enshrines the fundamental right to individual liberty, but at the same time a balance has to be struck between the right to individual liberty and NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/3022/2024 ORDER DATED: 15/02/2024 undefined the interest of society.
No right can be absolute, and reasonable restrictions can be placed on them.

While it is true that one of the considerations in deciding whether to grant bail to an accused or not is whether he has been in jail for a long time, the Court has also to take into consideration other facts and circumstances, such as the interest of the society."
9.

Thus, from the aforesaid decision, it is clear that Article 21 is of great importance because it enshrines the fundamental right to individual liberty, but at the same time, a balance has to be struck between the right to individual liberty and the interest of society.

As per the statement made by the victim girl that against her wish and will, on two to three occasions, applicant accused has used force and developed physical relationship with her, without going into further merits of the matter, at this stage, I am not inclined to entertain this application.
Accordingly, application stands dismissed.
Rule is discharged.
